page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor built on x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 35 MB of L3 cache. It features 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. Local ephemeral storage is absent, and network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Instruction extensions include AVX-512 foundation flags, AES encryption, FMA, and hardware virtualization via KVM.

Benchmark results show a clear variance between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. Single-core processing shows lower-tier performance, recorded at a 930.0 Geekbench single-core score and a 1109.68 stress-ng single-core result. However, multi-threaded operations scale into middle-tier performance metrics, achieving 8837.03 on stress-ng multi-core tests and 4693.0 on Geekbench multi-core workloads. Memory read bandwidth uncached achieves 59.2 GB/sec with write speeds reaching 49.35 GB/sec.

The high memory density relative to compute resources makes the ecs.se1ne.3xlarge instance suitable for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory caches, database operations, and software compilation tasks. Redis SET benchmark tests yield 8.48 million operations per second, while Passmark database operations score 3243.33. Single-threaded tasks, high-throughput static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference exhibit diminished relative throughput. The absence of local disk capacity requires attachment of external block storage for persistent data operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 12 dedicated vCPUs, 6 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores operating at 2.5 GHz, and 96.0 GB of RAM. Featuring an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation, it delivers a high memory-to-core ratio suited for memory-intensive applications without bundled local storage. Single-threaded benchmark performance sits in lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a 930.0 Geekbench single-core score. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU and memory operations perform in the middle 50% percentile, with multi-core stress-ng scores reaching 8837.03 and uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 59.2 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 8.48 million ops/sec. Network baseline throughput is rated at 2 Gbps. This instance provides a cost-effective operational profile for memory-heavy compute tasks, in-memory datastores, and enterprise database operations that rely on attached cloud block storage.
